title: CSI volumes left overs are not cleaned up if CSI plugin is attachable
body:
### What happened?

1. Create a Deployment or SS that uses a vsphere CSI volumes (for example).
2. Shutdown the node while pod was running.
3. Wait for node to go `NotReady` and pod to switch to `Terminating` state. 
4. Bring back the node up.
5. If the pod migrates to different node (or pod gets deleted), then files/directories inside `/var/lib/kubelet/pods/xxxx` should be cleaned up.

The reason those directories are not being cleaned up is because:

1. The volume types that are attachable, kubelet expects `node-publish-path` to be a mount point during reconstruction. So if node is rebooted then reconstruction fails because `/mount` path is not a mount point.
2. Kubelet tries to "Cleanup" the volume, but CSI driver may be unavailable at this point.
3. As a result volumes are never cleaned up.





### What did you expect to happen?

Expected cleanup to happen properly. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

See above

### What happened?

When running `kubectl logs pod-name --follow`, new logs are not output to the logs command after the log file has grown and rotated.


### What did you expect to happen?

Even after log rotation, new logs are output to `kubectl logs pod-name --follow`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

The following steps will reproduce it.

1. Deploy a Pod that continues to output to stdout.
2. Run `kubectl logs pod-name --follow`.
3. Wait a while and the log file will be rotated. The waiting time depends on the environment.

I have investigated this issue.
I found that when the problem occurs, it always goes through the same place and then there is a problem.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/897f2f78a5c7ff659dfce23f53dd36b9261a23c9/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/logs/logs.go#L351-L365

When a log file is renamed by rotation, `recreated` becomes true, but immediately after the renaming, `os.Open(path)` will result in a `Not Exist` error because the new log file has not yet been created.

Then it will re-loop by continue, but since `recreated` will not be true in the next loop, it will never enter this process again.
As a result, the log after log rotation will not be read.

/triage accepted

title: Windows Hostprocess containers can't use the InClientConfig for api access
body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:

If you try to access the api service using Inclusterconfig  with Windows hostprocess container you get an error:

```
open /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token: The system cannot find the path specified.
```

#### What you expected to happen:

Should be able to connect to the API server. This is common scenario for kube-proxy and CNIs.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: hostprocess-agnhost-older-client
spec:
  securityContext:
    windowsOptions:
      hostProcess: true
      runAsUserName: "NT AUTHORITY\\SYSTEM"
  hostNetwork: true
  containers:
  - name: test
    imagePullPolicy: Always
    image: k8s.gcr.io/e2e-test-images/agnhost:2.32
    command:
      - powershell
      - -c
      - start-process
      - "-wait"
      - "-nonewwindow"
      - "$env:CONTAINER_SANDBOX_MOUNT_POINT\\agnhost"
    args:
      - "inclusterclient --poll-interval 5"
  restartPolicy: Always
  nodeSelector:
    "kubernetes.io/os": windows
  tolerations:
    - key: ""
      operator: "Exists"
      effect: "NoSchedule"
---
```

```
kubectl logs hostprocess-agnhost-older-client
I0825 00:12:40.693662    5192 main.go:61] started
I0825 00:12:40.758659    5192 log.go:184] err: open /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token: The system cannot find the path specified.
```

title: glusterfs CSI migration support or deprecation needed
body:
CSI migration is an effort to enable smooth transition from intree volume plugin usage to CSI driver usage. 
Context: https://kubernetes.io/blog/2019/12/09/kubernetes-1-17-feature-csi-migration-beta/

Currently we are trying to evaluate for non-cloud provider plugins if they are in the interest of CSI migration support. If not, we will plan to mark them as deprecated and remove the source code from core kubernetes in the later releases.

For glusterfs, please let us know if CSI migration support is still in their roadmap or we should mark it as deprecated. 

/sig storage
/cc @msau42 @saad-ali 
/cc @humblec @jsafrane @gnufied

nodes.body:
For the users who wants to use glusterfs with CSI, there is an option available - https://github.com/kadalu/kadalu/

Hence for a large project like kubernetes, if glusterfs is the only volume plugin delaying the CSI migration, users can be pointed to kadalu project and glusterfs can be marked deprecated. @humblec is that fine?

meantime, from kadalu project we will see what we can do to help users migrate to CSI based deployment smoothly! (and would update this thread).

> For the users who wants to use glusterfs with CSI, there is an option available - https://github.com/kadalu/kadalu/

Yes, at the same time we got our initial Gluster CSI driver working a way back here https://github.com/gluster/gluster-csi-driver.
Just wondering or trying to find an opinion on whether we should revamp gluster CSI driver project itself. The advantage we get here is the smooth migration from in tree driver to CSI.  From the kube community and outside, we know many production deployments are running with in tree gluster drivers , so we have to really make a poll and take the call.

> 
> Hence for a large project like kubernetes, if glusterfs is the only volume plugin delaying the CSI migration, users can be pointed to kadalu project and glusterfs can be marked deprecated. @humblec is that fine?

Its not the case atm, but half of them migrated ( mainly cloud providers) and rest are getting planned on doing migration to CSI or marking `deprecated` . So we are left with some time but we have to make a decision without delay too.

> 
> meantime, from kadalu project we will see what we can do to help users migrate to CSI based deployment smoothly! (and would update this thread).

Thats one option as well, however considering both  models are bit different , we have to check is there a  possibility of smooth migration.

@Jiawei0227 I have kickstarted some discussions in the backend about our take on GlusterFS plugin forward. However I would like to officially take a survey/poll from a couple of communities atleast ( kubernetes and glusterfs) before we move on.  To take a feedback from kubernetes community, is there an official way of launching a Poll/Survey on deprecation of a plugin..etc? @saad-ali @jsafrane @msau42 @xing-yang  . I believe its important to take a decision based on community feedback  considering the plugin existed for long time ( since v1..4 or since 2016 https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/30888)  . Meanwhile we will also do the same from gluster community. 

@amarts can we trigger a poll from glusterfs community as well?  I can help on this as well.

> @amarts can we trigger a poll from glusterfs community as well? I can help on this as well.

Sure @humblec! Lets get a poll running in gluster mailing lists. We surely need to include heketi community (considering I see many users who only watches changes there, and not glusterfs) too. @phlogistonjohn @raghavendra-talur
I would suggest attending the next sig-storage meeting to sync with the community and get some initial feedbacks. And then probably a mailing list to sig-storage for a larger audience feedback.
/triage accepted
/assign @humblec
There is also https://blog.k8s.io/ and / or https://k8s.dev/blog/ to publicize the CSI driver migration generally and to highlight specific calls for participation like this.

title: volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node never cleared for non-existent nodes on PVC without PVs
body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:

* PVC was created, & pod consuming this PVC. PVC is using the WaitForFirstConsumer policy. 
* controller with SA `persistent-volume-binder` in `kube-system` namespace edited the PVC, attached the following labels:

```
    volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-provisioner: ebs.csi.aws.com
    volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node: ip-10-0-92-212.ec2.internal
```
* PVC is pending phase, it wasn't bound to the PV. 
* The node in question was deleted, by cluster autoscaler 1.20 before the PV was provisioned and attached to the node. 
* The annotation remains
* The https://github.com/kubernetes/autoscaler/tree/master/cluster-autoscaler v1.20 cannot scale up the node since there's the `volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node` annotation pointing to the deleted node. The cluster autoscaler sees this PVC bound to the Pod already bound to the node, but the node isn't there. 
* The pod stays forever in pending state
* Deleting this annotation allows cluster autoscaler to do its job, scaling up the cluster and the pod gets scheduled on a newly provisioned node. 
* The end. 

#### What you expected to happen:

* Upon node deletion, the `volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node` annotation should be cleared. 

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

* You're playing with race conditions, but the previously mention story should be sometimes replicable. 

#### Anything else we need to know?:

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
```
Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"19+", GitVersion:"v1.19.6-eks-49a6c0", GitCommit:"49a6c0bf091506e7bafcdb1b142351b69363355a", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2020-12-23T22:10:21Z", GoVersion:"go1.15.5", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
```

- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
- AWS EKS

nodes.body: /sig storage

/assign @verult @jsafrane

It looks like we only remove the selected-node annotation on provisioning failure if the [error returned is resource exhausted](https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/external-provisioner/blob/1b9d55dd8c7d8c076abeea1039d261723e2d6efa/pkg/controller/controller.go#L1717). Do you think it makes sense to return rescheduling for any other final error?

/triage accepted
@kubernetes/sig-storage-bugs

> Do you think it makes sense to return rescheduling for any other final error?

It makes sense removing this annotation if node in question does not exist anymore. If the underlying PV can be attached to some other node, like many cloud PVs can, then it should be allowed to do so.

Sorry, I somehow missed this issue.

> It looks like we only remove the selected-node annotation on provisioning failure if the error returned is resource exhausted. Do you think it makes sense to return rescheduling for any other final error?

I don't want a PVC + Pod to hop around Nodes on every little hiccup in the CSI driver. I think the provisioner should have at least configurable amount of retries (on cmdline). Then it could work for most CSI drivers.

For CSI drivers with the distributed provisioning mode, where each node runs its own external-provisioner, we need something else. If a node's VM is deleted (crashes, ...), there is no external-provisioner running for the node and therefore nothing removes the annotation. Since no in-tree controller (scheduler, PV controller) knows that there is distributed provisioning in action, they cannot remove `AnnSelectedNode`. Therefore it would need to be all other external-provisioners that would need to watch *other* CSINodes and clear the annotation from PVS that are scheduled to wrong nodes. I don't like it at all. @pohly, do you have any idea how to fix it?

In addition, when a CSINode is deleted / looses record of the CSI driver, can we be sure that the external-provisioner does not run on the node? If it was running, it can could be already provisioning a volume while say PV controller tries to remove the annotation, leading to weird races / possible volume leaks.

For the record, I think we could be fine in:
* Static provisioning (e.g. local volumes). I don't remember the binding sequence, do we set / clear `AnnSelectedNode` for non-dynamically provisioned PVCs? Scheduler / PV controller could be fine here.
* In-tree dynamically provisioned volumes. They're being moved to CSI soon.

> Therefore it would need to be all other external-provisioners that would need to watch other CSINodes and clear the annotation from PVS that are scheduled to wrong nodes. I don't like it at all. @pohly, do you have any idea how to fix it?

There is https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/external-provisioner/issues/544 for tracking that problem. The idea there is to have one central external-(de)provisioner which knows about nodes where the CSI driver should be running and clears the annotation for nodes where it doesn't run.

Implementing this is a bit tricky due to potential races and having to know where the driver is supposed to run. It's doable and I have implemented it [in PMEM-CSI](https://github.com/intel/pmem-csi/blob/49fe04e10793a82bb76b2ae7fe4c7c3eb55ccd86/pkg/pmem-csi-driver/rescheduler.go#L138-L200) based on the provisioner lib. It might be possible to generalize that and move it into external-provisioner.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

declare -A nodes

  if ! [[ ${nodes[$node]-} == "exists" ]]; then

done
```

title: Filesystem resize is required after snapshot restore / volume clone
body:
Kubernetes should resize filesystem on a volume when it's created as a clone of a smaller volume / smaller snapshot is restored into it.

Example:
1. User takes a snapshot of 1 GiB volume with ext3 filesystem on it.
2. User restores the snapshot into 2 GiB volume.
    2.1 CSI driver restores the snapshot into a bigger volume, but ext3 filesystem still uses only 1 GiB of space.
3. CSI driver should make sure that the filesystem on the volume has been resized before the volume is mounted into a pod.

There are few steps needed:

* [x] Clarify behavior of `CreateVolume` CSI call, https://github.com/container-storage-interface/spec/pull/452
* [ ] Update CSI drivers to the new behavior.
  * [x] Move filesystem resize code from kubernetes/kuberenetes to kubernetes/mount-utils, so all CSI drivers can re-use the same code https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/99039 
  * [x] Enhance the code above to compare the volume size from block device perspective and from filesystem perspective. See https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/aws-ebs-csi-driver/pull/595 for proof of concept. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/99042
  * [ ] File issues in all community CSI drivers that we care about & fix them.
* [ ] Update csi-tests to (optionally?) check for volume size when cloning / restoring snapshot to a bigger size. https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/csi-test/issues/325

nodes.body:
/assign
/sig storage
/priority important-soon
True, considering the CSI spec allows restore to a bigger size volume, we should have the support from CO.

> * Update the external-provisioner to create PVs that are marked for resize when a volume clone / snapshot restore is bigger than the original.

This is hard, Kubernets PV controller overwrites `PVC.Status.Capacity` on binding. 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8422044f1746354393ea5b617e2bde5c24c0f829/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/pv_controller.go#L771-L784

Therefore the external-provisioner cannot create PVC as "marked for resize on node", i.e. with `PVC.Spec.Capacity` = `PV.Spec.Capacity` = the real size of the new volume) and with `PVC.Status.Capacity` = size of the original volume.

We either need to change the binding mechanism not to overwrite `PVC.Status.Size` or add a flag (annotation?) that marks the volume for resize on node, even when `PVC.Spec.Capacity == PVC.Status.Capacity`.

Talked to @gnufied:

* The external-provisioner could mark `PVC.Status` for resize on node:
  * Set `PVC.Status.Capacity` to the original volume size.
  * Add `FileSystemResizePending` condition to the PVC.
  * As result, the extenal-provisioner needs to modify `PVC.Status`, which needs new RBAC and is a breaking change.
* The PV controller could respect `PVC.Status.Capacity`, if set.

We discussed and rejected adding a new flag / annotation to PV by the external-provisioner for kubelet to call NodeExpandVolume on the first mount. Such a flag would need to be cleared by  kubelet and kubelet can't modify PVs.

From latest discussion last week, I believe the conclusion was to have external-provisioner set `PV.Spec.Capacity` to the smaller size. Then we just let the rest of the normal resize flow continue. No need to have provisioner set the conditions.

@kubernetes/sig-storage-bugs

@msau42 we agreed to set conditions too because we want to be as close as possible to external-resizer. If there is some tooling that depends on condition for resizing pending on node, we don't want to break any such tooling. currently kubelet does not depend on condition for node expansion though.
Why can't we let resize controller set the condition when it sees pvc size != pv size?
@msau42 hmm good point. I think that should work but we may have to verify that flow.
I think we can do that, but only with a change to the CSI spec wording, because the current implication is that should not be necessary.
